title: Transit and shelter for a family displaced by flooding
story: The Anwar family left their village in the last week of August when the water reached the roof of their house. They are now in a school hall two provinces away with what they carried. Their land and their stored rice are under water and they cannot reach either, and the bus fare back plus three months of rented rooms is beyond anything they have. We are raising for the fare, a room, and bedding for six people including two grandparents. Their displacement registration and their identity papers have been shared with the campaign team.
reviewerNote: Approved. This is the shape our policy describes under the wayfarer heading: people away from home and cut off from assets they own but cannot reach, which is a different thing from owning nothing at all, and the copy is explicit about it. Registration papers were supplied and checked. I noted for the file that applying this category to displaced people is a reading our policy already takes and that our advisor signed off on this pattern of campaign last year, so I recorded the decision against that standing position rather than opening it again. Their land is not evidence against need here; it is precisely what they cannot reach. Worth saying plainly for the next reviewer: some platforms decline to verify traveller cases at all, on the practical ground that a genuinely stranded person is unlikely to be running a campaign. That is a workable position and it is not ours. We verify them where the displacement is documented, which is our board's choice about operating risk rather than anything scholars are divided on, and a reviewer who finds the documentation thin should say so rather than lean on the category being permitted.
